hints: Look at each statement separately, starting with what you know about the shape and bonding in ammonia.
Count the valence electrons around nitrogen in $\text{NH}_3$ and remember what happens when $\text{NH}_3$ meets water to form $\text{OH}^-$ ions.
Think about whether you need an acid or an alkali to release a basic gas from an ammonium salt, then combine which statements are true.
walkthrough:
**Check statement 1 - structure of ammonia**

Think of nitrogen with 5 outer electrons bonded to three hydrogens. That gives three N-H bond pairs and one non-bonding pair left on nitrogen.

$$\text{N} : 2,5 \rightarrow \text{NH}_3 \text{ has 3 bond pairs + 1 lone pair}$$

**Check statement 2 - ammonia in water**

Ammonia is a base. It accepts a proton from water to make hydroxide ions, so the solution becomes alkaline and pH rises.

$$\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{NH}_4^+ + \text{OH}^-$$

**Check statement 3 - making ammonia gas**

To liberate the basic gas $\text{NH}_3$ from $\text{NH}_4^+$, you need to remove $\text{H}^+$. That needs a base like $\text{NaOH}$ or $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$, warmed.

$$\text{NH}_4^+ + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Combine the verdict**

Statement 1 is true and statement 2 is true. Statement 3 is false because hydrochloric acid is an acid and will keep nitrogen as $\text{NH}_4^+$, not release $\text{NH}_3$. So only 1 and 2 are correct.

options.A: Incorrect. This option includes statement 3 as well as 1 and 2. Warming an ammonium salt with an acid cannot give ammonia, the acid supplies H+ and keeps the equilibrium as NH4+.
options.B: Correct. Statements 1 and 2 only are true. Ammonia has 3 bond pairs and 1 lone pair (pyramidal), and it forms OH- in water raising pH. Statement 3 is false as preparation requires a base, not HCl.
options.C: Incorrect. This combination includes statement 3 and omits statement 1. Statement 1 is definitely true from electron counting, while statement 3 is false because HCl is acidic.
options.D: Incorrect. This combination omits statement 2. Statement 2 is true because NH3 + H2O gives NH4+ + OH-, making the solution alkaline with higher pH than pure water.
